notes_for_editor: Only the tnlandforms list places this tower (32.354363,-84.933886; the record has 32.35436,-84.93389). Its listed elevation is 442 ft, which the record holds as 134.7 m. The note 'topo 1950 army' is unexplained in the list. A second lookout list (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/georgia.html) has one line 'FORT BENNING, Chattahoochee County' that does not say which tower, so it is not cited. NGS mark CM1885 'FORT BENNING FIRE TOWER' sits at about 32.3758,-84.8667, which matches the list's plain 'fort benning' entry (GA353), not this tower, so it is not used here. Access is left unset: Fort Benning is an active Army post and no source checked says whether this site is open to visitors; a human should confirm the rules before access is set. Lead not read: Garrow & Associates, Historic Preservation Plan for Fort Benning, vol. 2 (1995, UGA GASF report 14160); its PDF was not reachable from the cache and it may cover the post's towers. No build date, status or staffing found. Confidence low. The story no longer says visits must follow the post's rules; no source checked states it. The tnlandforms page does not name Tom Dunigan in the fetched text; the attribution is kept as in the other stories, unconfirmed on the page.
